answer: Bonded collateral makes equivocation costly: when \(k\) identities coordinate, pairwise evidence links create \(k(k-1)/2\) attributable interactions, so penalties scale as \(O(k^2)\), not merely with the number of keys. A canyon, ferrous, or timber label cannot hide common control; detection triggers correlated slashing and an exponential multiplier in capital loss, making a sybil swarm substantially riskier than one identity.
